name: Stony Point Campground (Chippewa National Forest)
note: Chippewa National Forest (USFS) campground on Leech Lake, 14 mi E of Walker; 44 sites with electricity, boat access, swimming beach. Walker Ranger District. --Claude

name: Ada Lake Campground
note: Chequamegon-Nicolet NF (Laona RD) on 75-acre Ada Lake. Majority fit 30 ft+, some 45 ft+. Swim beach, boat landing. Open ~May 2-Oct 15. --Claude

name: Pine Lake Campground
note: Chequamegon-Nicolet NF (Laona RD) on the western shore of 1,667-acre Pine Lake. 12 wooded sites; accommodates trailers 40 ft, most sites 45 ft+. Hand-pump well water, paved boat landing, swim beach. Listed on recreation.gov. (Distinct from the private Hiles-Pine Lake Campground.) --Claude

name: Lac Vieux Desert Campground
note: Chequamegon-Nicolet NF (Eagle River-Florence RD) on the west shore of Lac Vieux Desert (Wisconsin River headwaters). Boat landing, picnic shelter, beach. Back-ins. --Claude

name: Perch Lake Campground
note: Chequamegon-Nicolet NF (Washburn RD) on 72-acre Perch Lake ~5.5 mi N of Drummond. 16 sites in two loops (N loop 10 sites w/ boat launch+dock; S loop 6 sites), RVs up to 30-35 ft. --Claude

name: Stockfarm Bridge Campground
note: Chequamegon-Nicolet NF (Great Divide RD) on the East Fork Chippewa River. 7 single-family sites + 1 group site; max RV 45+ ft (site 8), site 6 to 40 ft, others 25-30 ft. Hand-pump water, boat launch. Season opens ~Thu before May fishing opener. --Claude

name: Pines Point Campground

booking.note: All 27 family sites are first-come. Only the 5-site group loop is reservable, on recreation.gov or at (877) 444-6777 (2-night weekend minimum, booking closes 4 days before arrival). Check-in 2 p.m., check-out 11 a.m. Run by a concessionaire (American Land & Leisure).

note: Manistee NF campground on the banks of the White River near Hesperia, quiet and secluded under towering white pines, several sites overlooking the river. Walk-in canoe landing (a 30-60 minute float around the point) and a day-use area. Reached via 168th Ave / FR 5637. --Claude

name: Mill Creek (Greers Ferry Lake)
note: USACE Greers Ferry Lake campground; 31 non-electric sites, boat ramp. --Claude

name: Erbie Campground (Buffalo National River)
note: NPS Buffalo National River, Upper District. 14 drive-in sites (plus 13 walk-in and 5 group sites); drive-in sites listed as accommodating RVs up to 35 ft. Flush restrooms + water spigots seasonal. ACCESS CAUTION: reached via ~6-7 mi rough, twisting, narrow graded gravel road with switchbacks and a hairpin off Hwy 7 north of Jasper - passable by a careful 23-ft rig but described as not suitable for larger RVs/trailers (no 4WD required, unlike nearby Kyles Landing). FCFS in season; reservations begin in fall 2026 for some sites. --Claude

name: Trail Creek Campground
note: Caribou-Targhee NF along Trail Creek near the WY/ID line at Teton Pass (~7 mi from Victor, ID), ~6,600 ft. ~10-13 tent/RV sites in a grassy meadow, gravel spurs; picnic tables, fire rings, food lockers, vault toilets, drinking water. --Claude

name: Atherton Creek Campground
note: Bridger-Teton NF campground on Lower Slide Lake in the Gros Ventre near Kelly; 20 sites, paved access. Picnic tables and fire rings; boat access and trout fishing on the lake. --Claude

name: Hunter Peak Campground
note: Shoshone NF (Clarks Fork RD), 10-site campground on the banks of the Clarks Fork of the Yellowstone River at ~6,500 ft on the Chief Joseph Scenic Hwy (WY-296). Hand-pump water, bear boxes, food-storage required. --Claude

name: Threemile Campground
note: Shoshone NF, Wapiti RD, on the North Fork of the Shoshone River ~3 mi from Yellowstone's east entrance (~50 mi W of Cody), ~6,650 ft. 21 sites; HARD-SIDED RVs/campers ONLY (no tents/pop-ups, grizzly area), sites to 35-75 ft, vault toilets, hand-pump water, bear boxes. --Claude

name: Wapiti Campground
note: Shoshone NF, Wapiti RD, on the North Fork of the Shoshone River ~30 mi W of Cody on the Buffalo Bill Scenic Byway, ~5,950 ft, by the historic Wapiti Ranger Station. 41 sites — sites 1-21 have 15/30-amp electric, 22-40 nonelectric; RVs to 35+ ft, bear boxes. Online reservations currently suspended. --Claude

name: Agua Piedra Campground
note: Carson NF campground on NM-518 in the upper Rio Pueblo canyon (Camino Real RD), sites across a Lower loop plus Loop A and Loop B. The two group shelters are reservable online. Per-site max RV lengths run ~25-36 ft, so it fits a 23-ft rig. Near the Rio Pueblo and Agua Piedra Creek (trout fishing). --Claude

name: Big Elk Campground
note: Caribou-Targhee NF on the Big Elk Creek arm of Palisades Reservoir (Forest Rd 262). Individual sites first-come, first-served; 3 group sites (A-1, B-1, B-2) reservable online. Vault toilets, drinking water, trash; aspens/Douglas fir ~5,700 ft; Big Elk Creek trailhead at CG. --Claude

name: Riverside Campground (Idaho City)
note: Boise NF (Idaho City RD) on the Middle Fork Boise River, ~0.5 mi from the historic town of Atlanta; 11 sites, no hookups, vault toilet. Access via narrow, rough FS Rd 268 (~68 mi from Hwy 21). --Claude

name: Hot Springs Campground
note: Boise NF, Banks-Lowman Hwy east of Garden Valley on the South Fork Payette River; single sites plus 3 reservable group sites, paved spurs; natural hot springs across the road. Group sites reservable online. --Claude

name: Silver Creek Campground
note: In Peace Valley along Silver Creek, Boise NF; ~25 mi N of Garden Valley via gravel forest road. 53-59 single-family sites in three loops (Valley Creek, Lower/Upper Peace Creek) plus two group sites; paved roads and paved parking spurs. Register/pay at Silver Creek Plunge store; group sites reservable online. --Claude

name: Kings Creek Campground
note: USFS Dixie NF, west shore of Tropic Reservoir at ~8000 ft, ~9 mi W of Bryce Canyon NP via a partly paved, well-maintained gravel road (good RV access). Tent/RV sites + 2 group sites; flush toilets, drinking water and dump station in peak season. Group sites reservable on recreation.gov. --Claude

name: Sand Flats Recreation Area
note: BLM land co-managed with Grand County, ~5 mi E of Moab on the slickrock; ~140 individual sites across several loops (most fit RVs to ~26 ft, 6 sites in Loop A to ~40 ft) plus 6 reservable group sites. Group sites reservable online. --Claude
facility_name: Sand Flats Recreation Area Group Campsites

name: Gold Bar Campground
note: BLM Gold Bar Recreation Site on the Colorado River along Potash Rd (SR-279), ~10 mi NW of Moab; 9 individual drive-in sites (back-ins to ~35 ft, one pull-through), plus 4 reservable group sites; boat ramp. --Claude

name: Maple Grove Campground
note: Fishlake National Forest (Fillmore RD) campground beneath red cliffs on Ivie Creek, ~4 mi W of US-50 on FR-101 (milepost 146). Several single sites plus 3 reservable group sites. Maple/cottonwood/oak shade; Rock Canyon Trail starts in the campground. --Claude

name: Manti Community Campground
note: Manti-La Sal National Forest campground beside Yearns Reservoir at ~7,400 ft, ~7 mi E of Manti on FR-045 (dirt, no high clearance needed but rough/bumpy with occasional boulders — navigable with trailers). 6 single sites plus a group site; vault toilets, no potable water. Footpaths down to the small reservoir; canoeing and trout fishing. Group reservable online. --Claude

name: Oak Creek Campground (Oak City)
note: Fishlake NF (Fillmore RD) campground in Oak Creek Canyon ~4.4 mi E of Oak City, ~6,000 ft, shaded by oak/maple/cottonwood along Oak Creek. 17 individual sites (upper and lower loops) plus 4 group sites; picnic tables, fire rings, grills, amphitheater/play field. Individual sites pay on arrival; group sites reservable online. --Claude

name: Gooseberry Campground (Manti-La Sal)
note: USFS Manti-La Sal NF on an aspen-covered hillside above Gooseberry Reservoir, ~1 mi north on FDR 124 off SR-31; 10 single sites plus a reservable group site, pack-in/pack-out. Group site reservable online. --Claude

name: Avintaquin Campground
note: Ashley NF atop Indian Canyon off US-191 between Duchesne and Helper at ~9000 ft among Douglas fir; several single-family sites plus one group site (#10), no water (bring your own). Access is narrow washboard gravel with a hill climb. For the 2026 season the family sites are first-come-first-served; the group site remains reservable online. --Claude

name: Browne Lake Campground (Ashley NF)
note: USFS campground next to Browne Lake in a high mountain meadow (~8,200 ft), Flaming Gorge RD, Ashley NF, reached via well-maintained dirt road (FR-221 area). Four accessible group sites are separately reservable online. Picnic tables, campfire circles. Fishing (rainbow/brook trout, kokanee) and non-motorized boating on Browne Lake. --Claude

name: Skull Creek Campground (Flaming Gorge)
note: USFS campground in the Flaming Gorge NRA (~35 mi N of Vernal, just W of the SR-44/US-191 junction) at ~7,400 ft in ponderosa/aspen on a hillside above Flaming Gorge Reservoir, Ashley NF. 17 single-family sites, each with picnic table and campfire ring; vault toilets; no drinking water; no hookups. --Claude

name: Greens Lake Campground (Flaming Gorge)
note: USFS campground on the shore of small Greens Lake (~7,470 ft) in the Flaming Gorge NRA, ~1 mi from cliffs overlooking Flaming Gorge Reservoir, Ashley NF. Lodgepole/ponderosa/aspen for partial shade; vault toilets, no hookups (dump stations and showers at nearby Deer Run/Lodgepole/Mustang Ridge). Greens Lake is non-motorized only (canoeing, trout fishing); Red Canyon Lodge is adjacent. --Claude

name: Greendale Campground (Flaming Gorge)
note: USFS Flaming Gorge NRA campground near the US-191/UT-44 junction, ~1 mi from Flaming Gorge Reservoir. 8 single sites (paved spurs, west of road) plus 2 group sites (dirt, up to 40 people, east of road); no hookups. Group sites reservable online. --Claude

name: Buck Creek Campground
note: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie NF (Darrington RD) primitive campground along Buck Creek in old-growth forest, ~16 mi up Suiattle River Rd (FR 26) from SR 530. 14 standard sites, large pull-throughs fitting big RVs (listed to 34+ ft), picnic tables and vault toilets, no drinking water, no hookups. CLOSED for the 2026 season due to flood damage to Suiattle River Rd (FR 26) - verify access before visiting. --Claude

name: Lookout Campground and Boat Launch
note: USFS Willamette NF (McKenzie River RD) campground and boat launch on the NE shore of Blue River Reservoir. ~20 undesignated camp sites (gravel) plus a paved boat launch, floating dock and day-use area; drinking water, vault toilets, camp host. Reservoir is drawn down late summer through mid-March. --Claude
facility_name: LOOKOUT CAMPGROUND AND BOAT LAUNCH - WILLAMETTE

name: Blackberry Campground
note: USFS Siuslaw NF campground on a wooded bluff over the Alsea River, ~18 mi east of Waldport on Hwy 34. 32-33 sites with paved spurs, picnic tables, fire rings. On-site boat ramp (drift boating, salmon/steelhead). --Claude

name: Nordheimer Campground
note: Six Rivers NF campground on the Salmon (Wild & Scenic) River near Forks of Salmon; ~12 family sites (fee area) plus 4 reservable group sites. The Salmon River Rd narrows to one lane with tight corners and cliffs past Butler Creek so larger rigs are discouraged, but it is a normal-vehicle (not 4WD) drive and the riverside flat fits a mid-size rig. --Claude

name: Mill Creek Campground (Bucks Lake)
note: Plumas NF campground on the northern arm of Bucks Lake (a PG&E hydro reservoir; FS-owned land operated by a PG&E-associated concessionaire). 10 sites (2 walk-in), some lakefront; max RV 27 ft; potable water, vault toilets, bear boxes. --Claude Bucks Lake drawn down below normal after Labor Day 2026 for dam repairs; boat ramps unusable from about mid-September 2026 (PG&E notice, 2026-10-10). --Claude

name: Sundew Campground (Bucks Lake)
note: Plumas NF campground on Bucks Lake (FS-owned land operated by a PG&E-associated concessionaire). 22 units, all with lake access/views; one accessible site; vault toilets (potable water intermittently out). --Claude Bucks Lake drawn down below normal after Labor Day 2026 for dam repairs; boat ramps unusable from about mid-September 2026 (PG&E notice, 2026-10-10). --Claude

name: Trumbull Lake Campground
note: Humboldt-Toiyabe NF campground at Virginia Lakes (~9,500 ft) beside 100-acre Trumbull Lake off Little Virginia Lakes Rd; ~30 non-electric sites including a designated RV site, drinking water and vault toilets, no hookups. --Claude

name: Hayden Flat Campground
note: USFS Shasta-Trinity NF campground on the Wild & Scenic Trinity River, Hwy 299 near Big Bar. Family loop (both sides of the highway) is first-come first-served; a separate group loop is reservable on recreation.gov. Tables/fire rings; drive-in, hand-carry boat access. --Claude

name: Curly Jack Campground
note: On the Klamath Wild & Scenic River off Curly Jack Rd near Happy Camp, Happy Camp RD, Klamath NF; 16 single sites (most fit ~24 ft, some to 40 ft) plus 4 group sites, shaded paved loops; individual sites first-come, first-served (groups reservable on recreation.gov). --Claude

name: Hemlock Campground
note: Modoc NF campground on the east shore of Medicine Lake (~6,700 ft) in the Medicine Lake Highlands; ~19 drive-in sites with tables, fire rings, grills, vault toilets and water hydrants (no hookups). Part of the Medicine Lake complex; cannot take large trailers but fits mid-size rigs. Sandy beach on the lake. --Claude

name: Sweetwater Campground
note: Stanislaus NF (Groveland RD) campground adjacent to Hwy 120 about 15 mi east of Groveland, near Yosemite's Big Oak Flat entrance; 13 units for tents and RVs. Cash/check. --Claude

name: Cherry Valley Campground
note: Stanislaus NF (Groveland RD) campground near Cherry Lake in the Hetch Hetchy watershed; 46 sites (41 single, 5 double), cash/check. Lake ~1.5 mi via trail; boat ramp near the dam. Reach via Cottonwood Rd from Tuolumne (Cherry Lake Rd is narrow/steep, not advised for RVs). --Claude

name: Big Meadow Campground
note: Stanislaus NF (Calaveras RD) campground on Hwy 4 ~25 mi east of Arnold, ~6,550 ft; individual sites plus a reservable group site; Lake Alpine and Spicer Reservoir a short drive away (not adjacent). Individual sites FCFS (cash); group reservable online. --Claude

name: Camp 9 Campground
note: Sequoia NF (Kern River RD) on the N shore of Lake Isabella, ~2,600 ft. 100+ single sites plus 11 reservable group sites, dump station ($25), fish-cleaning station, boat ramp. --Claude

name: Hole-in-the-Wall Campground (Mojave National Preserve)
note: NPS Mojave National Preserve campground at ~4,300 ft near the Hole-in-the-Wall Information Center. 35 sites with picnic tables and fire pits, pit toilets, water spigots, and a dump station; no hookups. Sites large enough for any size RV; paved access road. --Claude

name: Upper Oso Campground (Santa Ynez River)
note: Forest Service campground in Oso Canyon above the Santa Ynez River, off Paradise Road north of Santa Barbara; trailheads for the Santa Cruz Trail and the Aliso National Recreation Trail, and the Camuesa OHV route nearby. Only three sites take a trailer or RV (32 ft). PARTLY OPEN: 10 sites, the other 14 (mostly equestrian) closed after storm damage (FS, checked 2026-09-24). High river levels can close it in winter. --Claude
